When I first arrived in this country it was my grandfather who took me under his wing. Well, not mine, but my husband's grandfather. I had a rough time adapting to the new culture of consumerism and didn't understand the things that American's considered important. My husband and I met in South Korea. He was there as a soldier and I was flown in from the Philippines to perform a job that was described to me as “entertainer”. The other girls and I weren't prostitutes, but we were hired to sit with American soldiers and provide conversation with a woman. Conversation that wasn't free. We were essentially there just so that lonely men had someone to talk to for 20 minutes.

Brandon and I didn't hit it off initially, but he was persistent and eventually I came around. A short courtship later and things got more serious. He proposed. I accepted. After his tour in Korea had reached it's end, Brandon returned to the United States and I awaited for him to send for me. For many girls that's where the storybook romance ends, but he stayed true to his word and I relocated to yet another country further from my family. Brandon's grandfather, or Po-Pa as we called him, welcomed me to the family in a manner that never made me feel like an outcast. This white Texas family never did anything particular that made me feel uncomfortable, they welcomed me with embraces and made sure I was involved in all their family traditions. The differences came mostly in how I felt. Even when it seemed that some were judging me as if I took advantage of their soldier family member in his time of need, it never felt that way with Po-Pa.

Brandon and I had a child. A beautiful girl that bore my skin color. We were a happy family. Even though I missed my blood family there were plenty of moments to celebrate with Brandon's. Barbecues are popular in Texas and the summer heat doesn't seem to stop anyone from enjoying them. These gathering always brought my mind around to my family back in the Philippines, but Po-Pa wouldn't let me get down about it. I remember one time I was sitting at a picnic table just a little distance from the family, getting a moment of peace. While the rest of them enjoyed their celebration Po-Pa sat down next to me and started asking how my sister and mother were doing. I told him they were fine and that my father is happy that I am living here but that it also breaks his heart that I am so far away. It's funny how talking about the thing that is making you feel bad can also be what perks you up. It was nice talking to him about those things. He asked questions and listened intently. Everybody was so nice to me, but I love him differently.

Brandon disappeared one day. He just never came home. He left and I didn't know where. After a few very worrisome days, I learned that he was staying with one of my girl friends. Staying with her permanently. Romantically. I was devastated. Here I am, an immigrant with a child and no job to provide the necessities of life, including the place I was currently staying in. No family to run to, and no friend to take comfort in. When I felt the world was going to collapse, here comes Po-Pa. He babysat while I went looking for a job, he provided meals and clothes in our greatest time of need. When it came time to move out of the house, Po-Pa invited us to stay with him and Nana while I got things in order. He gave me advice on what steps needed to be taken to navigate the legal system involving divorce, child support, and my immigration status. The family never disowned me and would still welcome me into their homes, but somehow it was different around him. He seemed even more genuine about it.

It is with great pride that I can stand in front of you and say I am an independent woman. I have a place that I share with my daughter, a job for over a year, and a driver's license. None of that would have been possible without my grandfather. I love you Po-Pa, and may you find peace in your journey with angels. We will see each other again someday. Smile when you look down, for you made this possible. Although it is a day of mourning, let us remember him for his great generosity to those he knew, as well as to strangers from across the globe. Thank you.
